title: Binary search: closed interval
summary: Index of target in a sorted list, or -1. Closed [left, right]: return on a match, otherwise discard mid with mid + 1 or mid - 1. O(log n).
code: # Search a closed interval [left, right]; check mid, then exclude it.
triggers: does this exact value exist in sorted data, and where
any matching index will do, and a miss returns a sentinel
prompts: Issued ticket numbers are kept in sorted order. Check whether a presented ticket was really issued, and report its position.
A sorted list of employee badge IDs: find where a scanned badge appears, or report that it is unknown.
invariant: If target is present, it lies in values[left..right] inclusive; everything outside has been ruled out.
mantra: Closed interval: check mid, then step past it on both sides.
pitfalls: Closed [left, right] pairs 'while left <= right' with mid + 1 and mid - 1; half-open pairs '<' with right = mid.
With duplicates it returns some matching index, not the first; use lower bound for the first.
right starts at len(values) - 1 because right itself is still a candidate.

anchors.name: Search a 2D Matrix
anchors.trick: Treat the rows as one sorted list: index i is row i // cols, column i % cols.

anchors.name: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
anchors.trick: Same closed loop; first decide which half is sorted, then whether target lies in it.

mutations.explanation: Stops before checking the last candidate: [3] with target 3 returns -1.
When left == right and values[mid] > target, nothing changes and the loop never ends.
